insights.concise_text: KAR addresses the data hunger and noise robustness gap by using WordNet-extracted inter-word semantic connections to explicitly assist its attention mechanisms.

triple.subject: KAR
triple.object: the data hunger and noise robustness gap

insights.concise_text: The WordNet-based data enrichment method supplies the positional inter-word semantic connections that KAR uses to construct enhanced context embeddings for knowledge aided mutual attention.

triple.subject: the WordNet-based data enrichment method
triple.object: positional inter-word semantic connections for enhanced context embeddings

insights.concise_text: The hyper-parameter INLINEFORM6 limits semantic relation chains, thereby controlling how many inter-word semantic connections can be extracted as general knowledge.

triple.subject: the hyper-parameter INLINEFORM6
triple.object: the amount of extracted inter-word semantic connections

insights.concise_text: KAR's knowledge aided self attention uses pre-extracted general knowledge to restrict coarse-memory fusion to a precise subset of semantically connected passage words.

triple.subject: knowledge aided self attention
triple.object: pre-extracted general knowledge to restrict coarse-memory fusion

insights.concise_text: KAR's coarse memory layer uses knowledge aided mutual attention to produce question-aware passage representations, which the refined memory layer then transforms into final passage representations.

triple.subject: the coarse memory layer
triple.object: question-aware passage representations to the refined memory layer

insights.concise_text: KAR predicts answer start position and answer end position from refined memories, which are produced after knowledge aided self attention in the refined memory layer.

triple.subject: Answer Span Prediction Layer
triple.object: refined memories produced after knowledge aided self attention

insights.concise_text: The AddSent and AddOneSent adversarial sets evaluate the noise robustness problem caused by misleading sentences in evaluation examples.

triple.subject: AddSent and AddOneSent
triple.object: the noise robustness problem caused by misleading sentences

insights.concise_text: KAR is evaluated with Exact Match (EM) and F1 score on SQuAD 1.1, whose development examples are used to set INLINEFORM10 through cross validation.

triple.subject: KAR
triple.object: SQuAD 1.1 with Exact Match (EM) and F1 score

insights.concise_text: The paper's explicit general-knowledge utilization replaces the existing implicit vector-space encoding because that encoding cannot be understood or controlled.

triple.subject: explicit general-knowledge utilization
triple.object: the existing implicit vector-space encoding

insights.concise_text: WordNet is chosen as the knowledge base because the paper limits general knowledge to inter-word semantic connections and WordNet stores semantic knowledge.

triple.subject: WordNet
triple.object: the limitation of general knowledge to inter-word semantic connections

insights.concise_text: KAR explicitly uses WordNet-derived inter-word semantic connections as general knowledge to assist its attention mechanisms, and replacing those mechanisms lowers F1 on the development set, AddSent, and AddOneSent.

triple.subject: knowledge aided attention mechanisms
triple.object: F1 score of KAR on the development set, AddSent, and AddOneSent

insights.concise_text: KAR's explicit use of general knowledge is supported by the finding that increasing INLINEFORM0 from 0 to 5 raises knowledge amount while KAR performance peaks when INLINEFORM1 reaches 3.

triple.subject: general knowledge
triple.object: performance of KAR to first rise until INLINEFORM1 reaches 3 and then drop

insights.concise_text: KAR's explicit general-knowledge utilization is claimed to work better than the implicit encoding-based method using Wikipedia and ConceptNet because that best model's development-set EM and F1 are much lower.

triple.subject: explicit way to utilize general knowledge
triple.object: existing implicit way

insights.concise_text: The conclusion that KAR is superior in hunger for data is evidenced by KAR performing much better than SAN and QANet on the development set and adversarial sets with training subsets.

triple.subject: training subsets
triple.object: KAR superiority in hunger for data

insights.concise_text: The conclusion that KAR is superior in robustness to noise is evidenced by KAR outperforming state-of-the-art MRC models by a large margin on adversarial sets.

triple.subject: adversarial sets
triple.object: KAR superiority in robustness to noise

insights.concise_text: KAR's comparable performance with state-of-the-art MRC models is evidenced by development-set and test-set evaluation against five top-20 SQuAD 1.1 single MRC models.

triple.subject: development set and test set evaluation
triple.object: KAR comparable performance with state-of-the-art MRC models

insights.concise_text: KAR's explicit general-knowledge design is associated with both comparable standard performance and large-margin robustness gains on adversarial sets.

triple.subject: Knowledge Aided Reader (KAR)
triple.object: comparable performance with state-of-the-art MRC models and large-margin robustness on adversarial sets

insights.concise_text: KAR's advantage in hunger for data and robustness to noise is jointly supported by training-subset comparisons with SAN and QANet and adversarial-set comparisons with state-of-the-art MRC models.

triple.subject: KAR
triple.object: state-of-the-art MRC models in hunger for data and robustness to noise
